events.title: Continental Congress Votes for Independence
events.description: The Second Continental Congress voted in favor of Richard Henry Lee's resolution declaring the thirteen American colonies free from British rule. Twelve colonies voted in favor, with New York abstaining. The formal Declaration of Independence was adopted two days later on July 4.
events.significance: This vote was the actual legal act of independence for the United States; John Adams believed July 2 would be celebrated as the nation's birthday.

events.title: First Zeppelin Flight
events.description: The LZ 1, the first rigid airship designed by Count Ferdinand von Zeppelin, made its maiden flight over Lake Constance near Friedrichshafen, Germany. The flight lasted about 18 minutes and reached an altitude of roughly 400 meters.
events.significance: It demonstrated the viability of rigid airships and launched the era of Zeppelin passenger and military air travel.

events.title: Disappearance of Amelia Earhart
events.description: American aviator Amelia Earhart and navigator Fred Noonan vanished over the Pacific Ocean while attempting to fly around the world. They were en route to tiny Howland Island after departing Lae, New Guinea, when radio contact was lost.
events.significance: One of history's most enduring mysteries, the disappearance sparked massive search efforts and continuing speculation about their fate.

events.title: Civil Rights Act Signed into Law
events.description: President Lyndon B. Johnson signed the Civil Rights Act of 1964 in a televised ceremony at the White House. The law outlawed discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin and ended segregation in public places and employment.
events.significance: It was a landmark piece of legislation that dismantled legal segregation in the United States and reshaped American society.

events.title: Death of Ernest Hemingway
events.description: American novelist and Nobel laureate Ernest Hemingway died by suicide at his home in Ketchum, Idaho, at age 61. He had struggled with depression and declining health in his later years.
events.significance: Hemingway's concise prose style profoundly influenced 20th-century literature, with works like The Old Man and the Sea and A Farewell to Arms remaining classics.
